_doc: Readable notes of the Larch Hollow wilderness sites (each has the item note_<id> in items/wild.json). Every note advances its site's story and points at the route: a key, a detour, a drop.

defs.title: Cedar Ridge Lookout — Daily Log
defs.author: M. Teal
defs.body:
Aug 30. Smoke all down the Tamsin. Not fires, burning off. Plotted nine. District says stay at station.
Sep 2. Lights going out in Pell's Crossing, one house at a time, east to west. Bearings 214, 219, 223.
Sep 4. Abe Sorrell came up the switchbacks at dusk with a bite above his boot. Put him in the woodshed with the good blanket.
Sep 6. Abe isn't Abe. Nailed the stair house shut from inside, bolted the back, locked the gate behind me. The spare gate key still hangs on the woodshed nail. I couldn't go back down for it.
Sep 9. The ground hummed all night. Every light in the valley started walking toward my lantern. They broke the stair house window and came up as far as the gate. They're standing there now. They don't knock.
Sep 10. I plotted the bearings from the hum. Every line crosses in the same place, up north under the ridges. Not on the ground. Under it.
Sep 11. The Program frequency answers in numbers. I write them down. — M.T.

defs.title: Card on the Stair Gate
defs.author: Cedar Ridge Lookout
defs.body:
RELIEF CREW —
Gate stays locked. Spare key on the nail in the woodshed, left of the door.
Come up by day and call out from the landing so I know you're you.
— M.T.

(Scratched into the paint beside it, later:) DON'T

defs.title: Cook's Order Pad
defs.author: Dee Pruitt, Camp 4 cookhouse
defs.body:
Flour, 2 sacks. Lard, gone. Coffee, Walt says ration it.
Moved the office keys to the pantry nail like Walt asked. The brass one's the office.
The boys in the bunkhouse stopped asking for supper Tuesday. Walt says leave the trays at the drying-room door and don't knock, and he's moved in with them to keep watch.
If you're crew: the kitchen door sticks. Shoulder it.

defs.title: Foreman's Ledger
defs.author: W. Brody, Tamsin Timber Camp 4
defs.body:
PAYROLL HELD — 14 MEN — pending road.
Moved to the safe in my room at the bunkhouse. I'm sleeping over there with the sick, somebody has to.
QUARANTINE (bunkhouse): Halvorsen, Pike, Dumont, Dumont, Kees, Ruiz.
Drying-room door is the only way in, front's barricaded. Key in this desk. Safe key on the iron ring in the records room.

Handwritten under it: If the road opens, pay them anyway. Every one of them.

defs.title: Note in the Foreman's Room
defs.author: Walt
defs.body:
They knew me right up till they didn't.
Kept them in. Front's barricaded, side door's bolted from in here, drying room's locked.
If I'm one of them now don't let me out either.
Pay the boys. — W.

defs.title: Night Watch Log
defs.author: Larch Hollow Mill, night shift
defs.body:
0150 Big doors barred from inside. Crew in the lunchroom upstairs.
0215 Basement stairs barricaded after Kowalski went down for the fuses and didn't come up.
0340 Something walking on the log deck. Haul chain's still running.
0410 Gus says the only way to the office now is through the basement. Filer has the office key up in the filing room.
0455 The headsaw is running. Gus is drawing them off the lunchroom. God help him.

defs.title: Filer's Notebook
defs.author: R. Sato, head filer
defs.body:
Headsaw benched and tensioned. Last one I'll do.
Office key's on my board by the grinder. Whoever goes for the payroll, take it. The safe key is in Pruett's desk next door, top drawer.
The basement stairs are barricaded below. Use the dust chute by the headrig, it drops you onto the waste conveyor. Soft landing, mostly.
Don't make noise down there. They lie in the sawdust like they're sleeping.

defs.title: Warning on the Door
defs.author: the Rasks
defs.body:
DONT OPEN
HE TURNED. WE NAILED IT
HE ASKED US TO
GOD FORGIVE US
— R. & J. Rask

defs.title: Trapline Journal
defs.author: Arvid Lindqvist
defs.body:
Nov 3. Two marten, one fox on the upper line. Something's been at the beaver sets. Not a bear.
Nov 6. It was a man. What used to be one. Lost the hand finding out. Wrapped it. The Rask boys are scared of me.
Nov 8. Fever. Put the good things in the cache box at the foot of the bunk. The key is where I keep everything I can't afford to lose: smokehouse, on the nail inside the door.
Nov 9. Sets are still out in the yard and along the path. Watch your feet, whoever you are.
Nov 10. Told the boys what to do. They're nailing the door now. Good boys.

defs.title: Letter from Anders
defs.author: Anders Lindqvist
defs.body:
Arvid -
The company has moved me up the exploration road to run Field Station 2. Bunks, a core shed, a cook who can't. Good money for minding geologists.
Something has them spooked. Ted Brask came up from the step-out rig last week white as his shirt, and nobody has been near his core boxes since. Head office rings twice a day now. Yesterday a car with no plates came up the road and two men in town shoes walked the shed with Ted and drove off without signing the book.
If they tell you in town the company has had a spill, it hasn't. I'd know. I don't know what it has had.
Keep your sets off the creek below the portal till I write again. Don't ask me why. I'll tell you at Christmas.
- Anders

defs.title: Statement, Folded in a Glove
defs.author: Lars Engen, driller's helper
defs.body:
I was driller's helper on BH-7, the step-out hole off the 4 Level. I want this written by somebody who was there, because the company will say a spill and the government will say nothing.
We were at 1,411 feet in grey limestone when the rods dropped four feet into nothing. Warm air came up the string and the drill bay smelled like bread rising. Brask had us pull the core. White threads in every crack, soft as cotton, and they were on our gloves and in our hair before anybody thought to stop us.
The company had us drill three more holes round it to see how big the hollow was. It isn't a hollow. The rods went into open cave every time, and the cave runs under the whole valley. We breathed it for six weeks.
Brask is in their ward up at the field station. The rest of my crew walk the 4 Level in the dark. I came down here because this was the first door I could bar.
I have the cough. If you are reading this, burn the core boxes. Don't sell them to anybody.
- Lars Engen
